blocks.text: Milk left on the kitchen table in Lagos spoils by evening; the same milk in a fridge lasts a week. Firewood split into thin sticks catches quickly while the whole log smoulders. Both observations are about the same question: what makes a chemical reaction go faster or slower?

blocks.title: Rate of reaction
blocks.text: The rate of a chemical reaction is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time. It can be measured as the volume of gas produced per second, the mass lost per second, or the time taken for a fixed amount of change to occur.

blocks.markdown:
## Collision theory

For a reaction to occur, particles must **collide**. But not every collision leads to a reaction. A collision is only **effective** when two conditions are met:

1. The particles collide with energy equal to or greater than the **activation energy**, the minimum energy needed to start breaking bonds.
2. The particles collide with the correct **orientation**.

Everything that speeds up a reaction does so by increasing the frequency of effective collisions.

rows: More particles per unit volume, so collisions are more frequent
Particles are forced closer together, raising collision frequency
More particles of the solid are exposed for the other reactant to strike
Particles move faster and a far greater fraction exceed the activation energy
Provides an alternative route with a lower activation energy
Supplies the energy needed to start the reaction
blocks.caption: The factors affecting reaction rate and why each works

blocks.title: Why temperature has such a large effect
blocks.text: Raising the temperature does two things, but they are not equally important. Faster movement raises collision frequency only slightly. The dominant effect is that a much larger proportion of molecules now possess energy above the activation energy. As a rough guide, a rise of 10 degrees Celsius roughly doubles the rate of many reactions.

blocks.title: Catalyst
blocks.text: A catalyst is a substance that alters the rate of a chemical reaction while remaining chemically unchanged in mass and composition at the end. It works by providing an alternative reaction pathway of lower activation energy. It does not supply energy, and it does not change the amount of product finally obtained.

blocks.title: Interpreting a gas-volume graph
blocks.prompt: Excess marble chips are added to hydrochloric acid and the volume of carbon dioxide collected is plotted against time. The curve is steep at first, becomes less steep, then flattens out. Explain each part, and predict how the curve changes if powdered marble of the same mass is used instead.

steps.text: At the start the acid concentration is at its highest and the marble surface is fresh, so collisions between H+ ions and the solid are most frequent. The gradient, which represents the rate, is therefore steepest here.
As the reaction proceeds the acid is used up. Fewer H+ ions per unit volume means fewer collisions per second, so the curve becomes progressively less steep.
The curve flattens when the acid is completely used up. Since the marble was in excess, the acid is the limiting reactant and no more gas can form.
With powdered marble the same mass presents a far greater surface area, so many more carbonate particles are exposed to attack at any moment.
The powder curve is therefore steeper at the start and flattens sooner.
Crucially, it flattens at the same height. Surface area changes only how fast the reaction goes, not how much product forms, because the amount of limiting reactant is unchanged.

blocks.answer: The falling gradient reflects the falling acid concentration; powdered marble gives a steeper initial curve that levels off earlier but at the same final volume

items: Collect the gas evolved in a graduated syringe and record the volume at fixed time intervals
Stand the flask on a balance and record the loss in mass as gas escapes
Time how long a cross drawn under the flask takes to disappear as a precipitate forms, as with sodium thiosulphate and acid
Withdraw small samples at intervals and titrate them to follow a change in concentration
Follow a colour change with a colorimeter where one species is coloured

blocks.title: Rate versus yield
blocks.text: Examiners regularly test whether you can separate the two. A catalyst, a higher temperature or a finer powder changes how quickly the final amount is reached. Only changing the quantity of limiting reactant changes how much product is finally obtained.

points: Reaction rate is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time.
Reactions occur only when particles collide with sufficient energy and correct orientation.
Concentration, pressure, surface area, temperature and catalysts all raise the frequency of effective collisions.
Temperature has the largest effect because it raises the fraction of particles that exceed the activation energy.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy and is unchanged at the end of the reaction.
The gradient of a volume-time graph gives the rate; the plateau height gives the final yield.
